reason: Hosting cache rules are defined in firebase.json: private member and admin routes are no-store; public pages carry no private data.
Firebase Authentication SDK modules are loaded from Google's trusted CDN; the CSP permits only www.gstatic.com.
The deployed HTML comments are reviewed source annotations and contain no credentials, member data, or operational details.
TLS and HSTS are controlled by Firebase Hosting and Cloud Run, not this application's response configuration.
Public pages and anonymised aggregate statistics may be cached; private API and member responses set no-store.
Firebase Hosting may serve public static pages from its CDN cache; authenticated data is never a static response.
The explicit CSP permits Firebase's required script and connection origins, including the unavoidable inline Firebase bootstrap.
The site uses JavaScript progressively and is expected to be identified as a modern web application; this is a classification warning, not a vulnerability.
State-changing requests require a verified Firebase bearer token and a permitted Origin; no cookie-authenticated state change exists.
Versioned Firebase SDK modules are loaded from Google's CDN without SRI because their URLs are generated by Firebase configuration.
Cross-origin isolation would block required Firebase Authentication resources; private responses retain origin and no-store controls.
